blocks.x: girlfriend. What's that? Okay, so you're discharged. Yeah. And so now that you're out, what was the prospects of your life at that point? Well, my prospect was, yeah. Maybe I could back up a little bit. How did you view the Navy

and how did it change your life? Well, okay, yeah. The Navy, to me, the Navy was a big asset in me being who I am today. Because, like I said, I went in the day I made seventeen. I was a little kid with a child of mine and all this. And going into the service, then, I had three years on my own, you know, being my own man, under command of somebody. And that's why I think today that the service is good for some people because if you, first of all, if you can take orders, live with them, take orders and live with them, and then, you know, and then, because you're going to learn something in the service, and more so today. But if you can take orders, you know, first of all, when you take orders, just learn you how to be more of a person because we all have to take orders. This is part of our growing system. And this is what it did to me. And then meeting Mr. Johnson, too, and then I didn't mess around with the bad element of the fellas. See, there was a little bunch of us. We were considered the nice ones in the company. And so I just, I grew as a person in the service. And I think it's very influential in me being who I am today.
